what_it_does: Tiny mechanical systems like nanoscale sensors need to measure displacement (how far things move) but are plagued by electrical interference from surrounding circuits. This paper describes a chip that converts capacitive sensor readings into digital numbers with extreme precision—measuring things as small as 35 attofarads (35 billionths of a billionth of a farad) up to 500 picofarads. The key innovation is using a phase-domain delta-sigma modulator: the sensor first converts capacitance into a phase shift through filtering, then a high-resolution digitizer turns that phase shift into numbers. This two-stage approach naturally rejects both slow DC-level noise and fast 100MHz interference simultaneously, enabling the sensor to work on electrically floating (ungrounded) targets.
